answer: Sybil resistance here rests on stake-weighted identity caps: each agent must post a bond from locked capital, and the ledger counts a thousand sock-puppets as one voice. A bot farm splitting funds across fresh keys gains nothing, since voting power scales with bonded value, not headcount. To outvote one honest operator holding a river of collateral, an attacker must lock the same capital on every alias, then see it slashed and burned for coordinated misbehavior. Enrollment also costs a proof over a shared ridge of attestations, like chipping onyx: dear per seat.
